items.title: A section of a smooth morphism is a regular immersion and is a right inverse of the flat pullback bivariant class
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism p : P -> X of schemes locally of finite type over the base situation and a section s : X -> P, the lemma asserts two things: that s is a regular immersion, and that 1 = s^! o p^* in A^*(X), where p^* is the flat pullback bivariant class (statement lines 13434-13442). The first assertion is quoted, but the operator identity is proved by reducing to a single cycle class: since the assumptions are preserved by base change it suffices to show s^! cap p^*[Z] = [Z] for an integral closed subscheme Z of X (proof lines 13447-13450). After shrinking P to a neighbourhood of s(Z) one may assume p has fixed relative dimension r, so every component of p^{-1}(Z) has dimension n + r and p^*[Z] = [p^{-1}(Z)]_{n+r}; the key observation is that s(X) cap p^{-1}(Z) = s(Z) scheme theoretically and that this is a regularly embedded closed subscheme of codimension r, so the fundamental-class lemma for a regularly embedded divisor applies (proof lines 13451-13457). Recognising that the scheme theoretic intersection computes s^! on the class is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
